edwards_parade.name: Edwards Parade
edwards_parade.blurb: The big oval lawn at the heart of the Rose Hill campus, with Keating Hall on its east side and Freeman Hall to the south.

keating_hall.name: Keating Hall
keating_hall.real_entrance: The main entrance faces west, up the wide stone steps from Edwards Parade, under the tower.
keating_hall.blurb: The gothic building with the tall central tower on the east side of Edwards Parade, one of the biggest and most historic buildings at Rose Hill. Maroon banners hang beside the entrance at commencement.

dealy_hall.name: Dealy Hall
dealy_hall.real_entrance: The columned main entrance is on the west side, facing Cunniffe House.
dealy_hall.blurb: Academic building of dark stone with white trim, beside Rose Hill Manor Drive across from Edwards Parade. A Ram Van shuttle stop is on the drive by its east end.

hughes_hall.name: Hughes Hall
hughes_hall.blurb: Home of the Gabelli School of Business: five storeys of dark fieldstone with white-trimmed arched windows, a glass roof, and a glass entrance under a teal canopy. The Ram statue stands out front, by the Cunniffe Fountain.

freeman_hall.name: Freeman Hall
freeman_hall.blurb: Built in 1930 for physics, in gray Collegiate Gothic stone, on the south side of Edwards Parade next to the Seismic Observatory.

collins_hall.name: Collins Hall
collins_hall.blurb: Built in 1904: red brick with a white classical front. Home of Collins Auditorium, the theatre program and the philosophy department, on Edgar Allan Poeway.

thebaud_hall.name: Thebaud Hall
thebaud_hall.blurb: Built in 1886 as Fordham's science building, under a green copper roof, next to the old power-plant smokestack near the Bathgate Avenue entrance. Home of the Public Safety Office.

larkin_hall.name: Larkin Hall
larkin_hall.real_entrance: The entrance is on the north side, facing the walkway along Walsh Library.
larkin_hall.blurb: Built in 1927 for biology: gray Collegiate Gothic with a tower over the door, at the south edge of Walsh Lawn, east of Walsh Library.

mulcahy_hall.name: Mulcahy Hall
mulcahy_hall.blurb: The chemistry building, opened in 1969, at the east end of the south side of campus.

faculty_memorial_hall.name: Faculty Memorial Hall
faculty_memorial_hall.blurb: Academic building in the southeast corner of campus, near Belmont Avenue.

cunniffe_house.name: Cunniffe House
cunniffe_house.real_entrance: The front door faces east, looking onto the Cunniffe Fountain.
cunniffe_house.blurb: The oldest building at Rose Hill, the original manor house: a gray stucco centre with a white cupola, between pink-brick wings. Today it holds university administration offices. Its front looks onto the Cunniffe Fountain, with Hughes Hall next door.

spellman_hall.name: Spellman Hall
spellman_hall.blurb: Built in 1946 as a home for the Jesuits who serve Fordham and Fordham Prep. It has its own chapel, St. Robert Bellarmine. Between Keating Hall and O'Hare Hall.

admissions.name: Duane Library / Admission
admissions.blurb: Duane Library (1926) was Fordham's library until 1998. Now it's home to the Office of Undergraduate Admission, the place to start a campus tour. It's marked in maroon on the campus map.

mcshane_center.name: McShane Campus Center
mcshane_center.blurb: The student center, rebuilt in 2021 where the McGinley Center stood: tall limestone walls and a glass atrium. The Marketplace inside is the main dining hall at Rose Hill.

walsh_library.name: William D. Walsh Family Library
walsh_library.real_entrance: The entrances are on the north side, facing Walsh Lawn, under the tower.
walsh_library.blurb: The main library, in the southwest corner of campus, below its tall slatted tower. Not to be confused with Walsh Hall, a residence hall on the south side.

university_church.name: University Church
university_church.blurb: Fordham's church since 1845, in gray Gothic stone, beside the Jesuit cemetery on Bellarmine Road. Its altar came from Old St. Patrick's Cathedral and some of its stained glass was a gift from King Louis Philippe of France. Fordham is a Jesuit university, and everyone is welcome.

rose_hill_gym.name: Rose Hill Gymnasium
rose_hill_gym.blurb: Home of Fordham basketball since 1925, with about 3,200 seats: the oldest on-campus arena still used by a Division I basketball team. Its stone Gothic front has a tall pointed-arch window, and the Victory Bell stands just outside.

lombardi_center.name: Lombardi Memorial Center
lombardi_center.blurb: The Vincent T. Lombardi Memorial Center, named for the Fordham alumnus and football coach: Fordham's athletics and recreation building behind McShane Campus Center. Inside are an eight-lane pool and a fieldhouse with an indoor 220-meter track.

moglia_stadium.name: Moglia Stadium
moglia_stadium.blurb: The 7,000-seat grandstand and press box along Jack Coffey Field, home of Fordham Rams football. It's named for Joe Moglia (FCRH '71).

jack_coffey_field.name: Jack Coffey Field
jack_coffey_field.blurb: Fordham's football and soccer field, with FieldTurf and lights. The Moglia Stadium grandstand runs along its north side. In baseball season the same turf is also Houlihan Park: the diamond sits at the south end, and the outfield runs up over the football field.

houlihan_park.name: Houlihan Park
houlihan_park.blurb: Jim Houlihan Park at Jack Coffey Field, home of Fordham Rams baseball. It isn't a separate field: the diamond is laid on Jack Coffey Field's FieldTurf, with home plate and about 1,000 seats at the south end and the outfield stretching north over the football field.

murphy_field.name: Murphy Field
murphy_field.blurb: A lit FieldTurf field for soccer and football practice, entered through a stone archway with a bust of Cornelius Murphy, the student it's named for. Bahoshy Softball Field is right next to it.

bahoshy_field.name: Bahoshy Softball Field
bahoshy_field.blurb: Home of Fordham softball, beside the tennis courts and Murphy Field. Home plate is in the south-east corner by a paved plaza. It has an all-dirt infield and a FieldTurf outfield with the Fordham F, ringed by a red-brown warning track.

tennis_courts.name: Hawthorn/Rooney Tennis Courts
tennis_courts.blurb: Six tennis courts beside Murphy Field, shared by the Fordham and Fordham Prep teams.

victory_bell.name: Victory Bell
victory_bell.blurb: A campus landmark outside Rose Hill Gymnasium, on Constitution Row.

ram_statue.name: Ram Statue
ram_statue.blurb: The Ram is Fordham's mascot. Its bronze statue stands in front of Hughes Hall, by the Cunniffe Fountain.

cunniffe_fountain.name: Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe Fountain
cunniffe_fountain.blurb: A tiered bronze fountain in a round stone basin, on the paved plaza between Cunniffe House, Hughes Hall and Dealy Hall. A good place to meet friends between classes.

st_ignatius_statue.name: St. Ignatius Statue
st_ignatius_statue.blurb: A statue of St. Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, north of Hughes Hall.

archbishop_hughes_statue.name: Archbishop Hughes Statue
archbishop_hughes_statue.blurb: A statue of Archbishop John Hughes, who founded Fordham in 1841. It stands between Martyrs' Lawn and Cunniffe House.

seismic_observatory.name: Seismic Observatory
seismic_observatory.blurb: A small observatory building next to Freeman Hall, south of Edwards Parade.

memorial_garden.name: 9/11 Memorial Garden
memorial_garden.blurb: A quiet memorial garden near Thebaud Hall and the Bathgate Avenue pedestrian entrance.

martyrs_lawn.name: Martyrs' Lawn
martyrs_lawn.blurb: The big lawn on the residential west side of campus, surrounded by Martyrs' Court and other residence halls.

walsh_lawn.name: Walsh Lawn
walsh_lawn.blurb: The lawn in front of the Walsh Family Library, crossed by Old Elm Road.

ohare_hall.name: O'Hare Hall
ohare_hall.blurb: Opened in 2000 and named for former president Joseph A. O'Hare, S.J.: three wings for up to 560 upperclass students, on the east side near the Main Entrance. It also houses important student services.

tierney_hall.name: Tierney Hall
tierney_hall.blurb: Three-storey upperclass hall next to O'Hare, built in 1986 as Sesquicentennial Hall.

queens_court.name: Queen's Court
queens_court.blurb: Three Collegiate Gothic halls (Bishops', St. John's and St. Robert's), joined as Queen's Court in 1940 round a garden courtyard with a statue. Home to a first-year wellness community.

alumni_court_south.name: Alumni Court South
alumni_court_south.blurb: One of the biggest first-year halls, on the far west side near the library and a Ram Van stop. Loschert Hall is its twin.

martyrs_court.name: Martyrs' Court
martyrs_court.blurb: Built in 1950 and named for Jesuit martyrs including St. Isaac Jogues. A first-year hall with study commons on every floor; its front steps are a favourite place to hang out.

loschert_hall.name: Loschert Hall
loschert_hall.blurb: First-year hall, formally Alumni Court North (1987), named for alumnus William J. Loschert. Its twin, Alumni Court South, is right next door.

faber_hall.name: Faber Hall
faber_hall.blurb: First-year hall: the seven-storey 1963 addition to Loyola Hall, first built as a Jesuit residence. The modern languages department is here too.

loyola_hall.name: Loyola Hall
loyola_hall.blurb: Built in 1936 for Jesuit faculty and named for St. Ignatius Loyola. Now a first-year hall, home to the Manresa program.

conley_salice.name: Conley & Salice Halls
conley_salice.blurb: Two upperclass halls on Mill River Road, opened in 2009 with Campbell Hall.

campbell_hall.name: Campbell Hall
campbell_hall.real_entrance: The dining entrance is on the east side, facing Mill River Road, near the Webster Avenue gate.
campbell_hall.blurb: A newer residence hall: modern dark brick with glass stair towers, between Archer Drive and Mill River Road, near the Webster Avenue gate.

finlay_hall.name: Finlay Hall
finlay_hall.blurb: Built in 1913 for Fordham's medical school, later a science building, now a hall mostly for sophomores. On Clavius Way near the Bathgate Avenue entrance.

walsh_hall.name: Walsh Hall
walsh_hall.blurb: Thirteen storeys on East 191st Street, opened in 1972 (first known as the "555"), with apartments for upperclass students. Not the library! That's the Walsh Family Library in the southwest corner.

ram_van.name: Ram Van Shuttle Stop
ram_van.blurb: Campus shuttle stops are marked with maroon bus signs. Rose Hill stops include Rose Hill Manor Drive by Dealy Hall, Edgar Allan Poeway by Cunniffe House, the Alumni Court circle, the Fordham Regional Parking Facility, and two on Mill River Road: at Old Elm Road, and by the Webster Avenue gate.

regional_parking.name: Fordham Regional Parking Facility
regional_parking.blurb: Parking garage on the east side of campus. Ram Van pick-up and drop-off is here.

parking_lot.name: Parking Lot
parking_lot.blurb: Surface parking just inside the Main Entrance, off Xavier Way. Parking on campus needs a Fordham permit, and visitors check in at the gate.

main_entrance.name: Main Entrance
main_entrance.blurb: The main vehicle entrance on Southern Boulevard, across from the New York Botanical Garden. Xavier Way leads from here to Matteo Ricci Circle.

webster_gate.name: Third / Webster Avenue Gate
webster_gate.blurb: The southwest gate. The Fordham Metro-North station is just outside, and the Fordham Road subway station is on Webster Avenue. A guard checks IDs here: tap your Fordham ID card, or your phone with Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.

bathgate_gate.name: Pedestrian Entrance (Bathgate Ave)
bathgate_gate.blurb: Pedestrian entrance at the south end of Rose Hill Manor Drive, by Thebaud Hall and Finlay Hall.

clavius_gate.name: Pedestrian Entrance (Clavius Way)
clavius_gate.blurb: Pedestrian entrance at the east end of Clavius Way, near Tierney Hall.
